Courage is often defined as the ability to do something despite feeling afraid. It's about facing fear and acting in a way that's brave. But courage can take many forms. Sometimes it's about confronting a situation head-on, like standing up to a bully or rushing into a burning building to save someone. Other times, it's about making the decision to avoid harm, even if that means not confronting the situation directly. In this scenario, James chose to duck under the counter and play possum when a burglary was happening. So, he didn't confront the burglar. Instead, he hid to protect himself. Is that courageous? But if hiding was the safest option, then that might be the better choice. I also remember that in Islamic teachings, there's a balance between courage and wisdom. Sometimes, wisdom dictates that avoiding a confrontation is the better course of action. For example, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) taught that if someone can avoid a situation through wisdom, they should do so. So, in this case, James using wisdom to protect himself could be seen as a form of courage. Another angle is the idea of courage in the face of fear. James was likely afraid during the burglary.
